incident: IcedID to Conti ransomware (zip/JS phishing to domain-wide Conti)

sources.title: Conti Ransomware - The DFIR Report (2021-05-12)
sources.what_it_gave: entry (phishing zip + JS -> IcedID via rundll32), hops (beacon over SMB/ADMIN$ to DCs, PsExec Beacon DLL to most systems, RDP proxied through IcedID), cred access (GetSystem, LSASS on multiple hosts incl DC, overpass-the-hash), impact (Conti in memory domain-wide, DC unrecoverable), 2d11h

narrative_before: In an April 2021 intrusion the DFIR Report assessed initial access was a phishing zip containing a malicious JavaScript file that downloaded and ran IcedID via rundll32 on the beachhead host (beaconing over 443). After more than two days dormant, a Cobalt Strike Beacon was dropped; hands-on activity lasted about two and a half hours on a Saturday morning. The actors got SYSTEM on the beachhead via Cobalt Strike GetSystem, accessed LSASS on multiple hosts including a domain controller, and used overpass-the-hash for a Kerberos ticket. Beacons were moved to domain controllers over SMB (ADMIN$ service binaries); a DC ran port scanning and dsquery, Cobalt Strike enabled RDP/firewall rules, and a local 'nuuser' account was added to Administrators on a DC. A Beacon DLL was pushed to most systems via PsExec and RDP was proxied through the IcedID process. About two and a half hours after hands-on, Conti was loaded as a DLL and executed in memory domain-wide (scanning 445/SMB); multiple machines including a domain controller were unrecoverable, with a 150k demand. Time to domain-wide ransomware was two days and 11 hours.

detection_moments.description: IcedID running on the beachhead and beaconing; >2 days dormant before Cobalt Strike Beacon dropped.
detection_moments.evidence: 'a zip file, which included a malicious JavaScript file ... IcedID ran via rundll32.exe and beaconed over port 443 for the whole intrusion' - Conti Ransomware, The DFIR Report

detection_moments.description: Hands-on: SYSTEM via GetSystem, LSASS accessed on multiple hosts incl a DC, overpass-the-hash; beacons moved to DCs over SMB.
detection_moments.evidence: 'LSASS: Accessed by runonce.exe on multiple hosts, including a domain controller ... Overpass-the-hash was used to get a Kerberos ticket' - Conti Ransomware

detection_moments.description: ~2.5h after hands-on: Conti loaded as a DLL and executed in memory domain-wide (scans 445/SMB); DC among unrecoverable hosts.
detection_moments.evidence: 'Conti, loaded as a DLL and executed in memory ... scans the network for 445/SMB, looking for machines to encrypt ... Multiple machines ... including a domain controller were unrecoverable' - Conti Ransomware

attack_path: phishing zip + malicious JavaScript downloads/runs IcedID via rundll32 (T1566.001/T1204.002)
Cobalt Strike Beacon moved to DC over SMB (ADMIN$ service binary); LSASS accessed (T1021.002/T1003.001)
PsExec copies Beacon DLL to ADMIN$ and runs it with rundll32 on most systems (T1021.002)
ambiguities: Hosts named by role only; victim sector not stated. 'Most of the systems' modelled as srv_1/pc_2/pc_3.
Number of DCs: the report references domain controllers (plural); modelled as two.
No exfiltration described. Domain admin not explicitly confirmed (nuuser added to Administrators).
Moments are the report's activity markers (IcedID, hands-on cred access, encryption), not a defender detection timeline.
